policies.title: Malian ordinary passports: Grenada advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Grenada's currently linked official nationality schedule lists Mali as requiring a visa prior to arrival.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Malian passport holder travelling as a short visitor.
The active Embassy schedule was updated April 2024 and should be rechecked if Grenada publishes a replacement.
Work, study, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and final-admission treatment are outside scope.

policies.title: Malian ordinary passports: Panama authorized visitor visa
policies.summary: Panama's live Embassy schedule lists Mali in the authorized-visa cohort, requiring advance consular approval unless the separate third-country-document waiver applies.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Malian passport holder travelling as a short visitor who does not qualify for Panama's separate third-country visa or residence waiver.
Apply in person at the competent Panamanian consulate before travel; the Embassy says approval may take up to 60 business days.
Work, residence, transit, special documents, consular-jurisdiction requirements and final admission remain outside scope.

application.label: Panama Embassy authorized-visa instructions
application.processingTime: Up to 60 business days, depending on document verification and completion.
steps: Determine that Panama's separate third-country visa or residence waiver does not apply.
Submit the authorized-visa documents in person to the competent Panamanian consulate before travel.
Travel only after the consular visa has been granted and carry all required supporting documents.

conflicts.explanation: The current full suspension preserves valid-visa grandfathering, specified exceptions and case-by-case waivers, so it cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The full suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes Puerto Rico. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.

The full suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes the U.S. Virgin Islands. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.

PP10998 fully suspends ordinary visitor entry and visa issuance for Malian nationals outside the United States without a valid visa on 1 January 2026, subject to exceptions and waivers that cannot be normalized.
The PP10998 full suspension cannot be normalized for Puerto Rico because the INA geographic definition treats it as United States and exceptions remain case-specific.
The PP10998 full suspension cannot be normalized for Guam because the INA geographic definition treats it as United States and exceptions remain case-specific.
The PP10998 full suspension cannot be normalized for the Northern Mariana Islands because the INA geographic definition treats them as United States and exceptions remain case-specific.
The PP10998 full suspension cannot be normalized for the U.S. Virgin Islands because the INA geographic definition treats them as United States and exceptions remain case-specific.
